messages:
sophie (support): Customer reports intermittent 502s to hosted inference in eu-west-1 starting ~2026-03-17T08:12Z, ~15% of requests for ~30m. They attached a short trace and curl output.
ali (eng-infra): Any cert, DNS, or routing change around that window?
ingrid (oncall): deploy-bot shows a cert rotation started 2026-03-17T08:10:57Z and completed 2026-03-17T08:11:35Z.
deploy-bot: Certificate rotation completed for edge-eu at 2026-03-17T08:11:35Z.
kevin (custops): Customer correlates errors ~08:11->08:40. They reran and still hit 502s sometimes.
sophie (support): Quick repro they gave: curl -v "https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/predict" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' -> returns 502.
ali (eng-infra): Can you paste their DNS trace? specifically any SERVFAIL/NXDOMAINs from their upstream resolver?
sophie (support): Their trace shows intermittent SERVFAIL from their corporate resolver between 08:09:58 and 08:12:10. Downstream dig against our authoritative returns both A and CNAMEs.
ali (eng-infra): Please run a quick local dig from a probe node: dig +short @1.1.1.1 svc.edge.eu-west-1.redwood.ai
sophie (support): Output from probe:
```
1.2.3.4
1.2.3.4
```
ali (eng-infra): Ok. Any evidence of mismatched CNAME chains or old cert chains?
ingrid (oncall): Looking at gateway logs: several TLS handshakes aborted with SNI-related errors during the rotation window. Snippet:
```
[08:11:12] TLS handshake failed: alert handshake_failure (client_hello SNI mismatch)
[08:11:14] connection reset by peer during TLS handshake
```
kevin (custops): Customer trace also shows intermittent TCP RSTs around the same times.
sophie (support): Hypothesis: resolver warmup + certificate rotation -> some clients saw stale CNAME/resolver answers mapping to nodes that had different cert chain ordering, causing SNI mismatch.
ali (eng-infra): We also briefly enabled stricter SNI validation flag in rolling canary yesterday; rollout reached ~30% by 08:10 and 100% by 09:00. That lines up.
ingrid (oncall): Action items: 1) Roll back strict-sni flag to 0% now. 2) Ensure cert chain ordering normalized across nodes. 3) Ask customer to flush local DNS cache or switch to public resolver as mitigation.
sophie (support): Can runtime/infra confirm rollback ETA?
ali (eng-infra): Rolling back strict-sni flag to 0% now (command: ./ops/flags set runtime.strict_sni 0 --env=prod --region=eu). I'll post when done.
ali (eng-infra): rollback done at 2026-03-17T08:18:50Z, propagation ~2m.
ingrid (oncall): Runtime team will follow-up with a patch to avoid mixed-chain states during rotation and add a watcher for resolver SERVFAIL spikes during cert events.
kevin (custops): I'll update the customer: explain root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps (DNS flush / use 8.8.8.8), and we've rolled back strict-sni. Offer to monitor and reopen if they still see >1% errors.
sophie (support): Thanks — marking this as high-priority escalation until monitoring shows normal error rates. :thumbsup:
